protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map pcr-01. 8 of 8 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3). Reading of the request: 8 reactions.

Labware for the technique (PCR setup): 1 finding.
1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 44:  p300.dispense(20, plate[well])
   The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 3: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 55:  p20.mix(3, 15, plate[dst])  # 3 cycles of 15 ul
   At line 55 the p20_single_gen2 draws 15 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm above
   the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 25 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate
   200 µL Flat reaches only 0.79 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line
   did it 24 times; 360 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow
   the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed.
   Source wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [1a7cf4ac7f77]

2. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 8 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 44:  p300.dispense(20, plate[well])
   At line 44 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   3), and 8 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [0b7785ae33a1]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 8 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and
4 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 53:  p20.dispense(5, plate[dst])
   At line 53 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 4 more to wells A1,
   B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it
   8 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the
   run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is
   usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 after line 53: `mix_after=(5,
   20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what
   the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [2ea84b47fc3d]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.

findings.title: 8 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 4 more went in (20% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 53 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 4 more to wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it 8 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3 after line 53: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
